newsitem.title: USA: ValuJet to resume flights to three cities with $49 fare.
newsitem.headline: ValuJet to resume flights to three cities with $49 fare.

text.p: ValuJet Inc. said Monday that it will resume service on Dec. 19 between Atlanta and Dallas/Fort Worth, West Palm Beach, Fla., and Fort Myers, Fla., at introductory rates as low as $49 one-way.
The low-cost carrier also said it will add 10 additional daily, nonstop flights between Atlanta and Orlando, Fort Lauderdale and Tampa as well as Chicago and Washington, D.C.
With this additional service, ValuJet will operate 128 peak daily system departures to 20 cities.

ValuJet President Lewis Jordan first disclosed the new fares in an interview Monday with NBC affiliate WXIA-TV, and said the airline's expansion plans remained on tract despite last week's National Transportation Safety Board hearings into the May 11 crash of ValuJet flight 592.

The carrier has slowly rebuilt service since it resumed service in October after being grounded for three months by Federal authorities as a result of a probe into the crash in the Florida Everglades that killed 110 people.
But the airline has only a fraction of service compared with the 320 daily flights to 31 cities it offered before its grounding.
Also on Monday, ValuJet was set to begin offering special fares of $39, $49, $59 and $69 to all its destinations for travel between Dec. 3 through Dec. 18.
